Baytril™ Taste Tabs™ Antibacterial Tablets

indication.text: Treatment of dermal infections (wounds and abscesses), respiratory infections (pneumonia, tonsilitis, rhinitis) and urinary cystitis in dogs caused by susceptible strains of E. coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Proteus mirabilis and Staphylococcus aureus.
indication.quote: Baytril® (brand of enrofloxacin) Antibacterial Tablets are indicated for the treatment of the following bacterial infections in dogs: Dermal infections (wounds and abscesses) caused by susceptible strains of Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae*, Proteus mirabilis and Staphylococcus aureus. Respiratory infections (pneumonia, tonsilitis, rhinitis) caused by susceptible strains of Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus.

dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: continued for two to three days beyond cessation of clinical signs, to a maximum of ten days
dose_regimen.quote: The optimum oral dose of Baytril® (brand of enrofloxacin) Tablets has been established at 2.5 mg/kg (1.13 mg/lb) of body weight administered twice daily.

pharmacokinetics.value: 1 hour (50% of maximum serum concentration within 15 minutes)
pharmacokinetics.conditions: 2.5 mg/kg oral, healthy adult dogs (12 dogs in 3 groups of 4; three dose levels, oral and IV)
pharmacokinetics.quote: At the recommended dose of 2.5 mg/kg (1.13 mg/lb) given orally, it reached 50% of its maximum serum concentration within 15 minutes and peak concentration occurred in 1 hour.

pharmacokinetics.value: greater than 3 hours
pharmacokinetics.conditions: oral and intravenous doses (1.25, 2.5, 5.0 mg/kg)
pharmacokinetics.quote: The half-life was greater than three (3) hours with both oral and intravenous doses.

pharmacokinetics.value: approximately 80%
pharmacokinetics.conditions: oral tablet vs intravenous
pharmacokinetics.quote: Approximately 80% of the orally administered dose entered the systemic circulation unchanged.

pharmacokinetics.value: approximately 9 ml/min/kg
pharmacokinetics.conditions: same at each dose rate (1.25, 2.5, 5.0 mg/kg)
pharmacokinetics.quote: The body clearance time was the same (approximately 9 ml/min/kg) at each dose rate

pharmacokinetics.value: plasma enrofloxacin 0.67 / 0.55 / 0.36 mcg/mL
pharmacokinetics.conditions: Table 14 tissue distribution study; single oral dose 2.5 mg/kg; columns are 2.0, 4.0 and 8.0 hours after dosing; n=6 through 2 h, n=4 at 4 h, n=2 at 8 h

pharmacokinetics.value: urine enrofloxacin 43.05 / 33.30 / 55.35 mcg/mL
pharmacokinetics.conditions: Table 14; single oral dose 2.5 mg/kg; columns are 2.0, 4.0 and 8.0 hours after dosing

pharmacokinetics.value: liver enrofloxacin 3.02 / 2.21 / 1.36 mcg/g
pharmacokinetics.conditions: Table 14; single oral dose 2.5 mg/kg; columns are 2.0, 4.0 and 8.0 hours after dosing; n=2 per interval

pharmacokinetics.value: skin enrofloxacin 0.66 / 0.80 / 0.48 mcg/g
pharmacokinetics.conditions: Table 14; single oral dose 2.5 mg/kg; columns are 2.0, 4.0 and 8.0 hours after dosing; n=2 per interval

target_animal_safety.n_animals: 16 adult dogs (4 per treatment group plus 4 controls)

findings.finding: No treatment-related adverse effects at 1X, 3X or 5X for 30 days except slight loss of appetite and depression at elevated doses
findings.quote: No treatment related adverse effects were observed in any of the parameters except for slight loss of appetite and depression in the dogs receiving the elevated treatments.

findings.finding: Drug tolerance study: 125 mg/kg/day caused vomition, inappetence, depression and death (days 10 and 11) in 2 dogs; 50 mg/kg/day caused infrequent vomition
findings.quote: The 125 mg/kg (56.7 mg/lb) treatment induced vomition, inappetence, depression and death in these 2 dogs with death occurring on Days 10 and 11.

findings.finding: Older puppies (19-28.5 weeks) dosed 5, 15 or 25 mg/kg/day for 30 days: lameness at 25 mg/kg and dose-related articular cartilage lesions in all treated groups
findings.quote: Clinical signs of lameness were observed in the 25 mg/kg (11.34 mg/lb) treated group. Histological lesions of the articular cartilage were observed in all treatment groups and the effects were dose related.

findings.finding: Rapidly growing large-breed puppies (10-12 weeks) at 10 mg/kg/day for 10-14 days: abnormal foreleg carriage and articular cartilage lesions
findings.quote: This controlled study confirmed this dosage rate can induce abnormal carriage of the foreleg and histological lesions of the articular cartilage in this age of rapidly growing large type breeds of dogs.

target_animal_safety.design_quote: M. Kohlenberg of Shawnee Mission, Kansas conducted a study in 16 adult, male and female dogs of various breeds with daily treatments at the use rate of 5 mg/kg/day (2.27 mg/lb/day). 3X use rate and 5X use rate for 30 days or 3 times the labeled duration. Four dogs were included in each treatment group plus 4 controls.

effectiveness.design: Pivotal well-controlled, blinded multi-investigator (10 sites) clinical field trial; dogs with dermal, enteric, respiratory or urinary tract infections randomized to enrofloxacin 2.5 mg/kg BID or Tribrissen 26.4 mg/kg SID orally for 5-10 days (positive control)
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: clinical response (pre- vs post-treatment clinical scores) and bacteriological response (pathogen elimination)
effectiveness.result: Clinically significant reductions in post-treatment scores with no medically significant difference between groups; pathogen elimination 70% (enrofloxacin) vs 67% (Tribrissen); by organism 80% vs 72%
effectiveness.quote: A total of 107 enrofloxacin and 78 Tribrissen® treated dogs (96 male and 89 female) of various breeds, ages (6 wks to 23 yrs) and weights were included in the study.

adverse_reactions.term: vomition, apparently drug related (clinical field trial safety evaluation, 270 dogs)
adverse_reactions.quote: Two of the 270 (0.7%) treated with enrofloxacin tablets in the clinical field trials exhibited side effects, which were apparently drug related. These 2 cases of vomition were self-limiting.

adverse_reactions.term: vomition, judged probably not drug related
adverse_reactions.quote: These observations were classified as mild, self-limiting and consisted of 2 incidents of vomition, 2 of depressed appetite and 2 of either diarrhea or soft stool.

adverse_reactions.term: depressed appetite, judged probably not drug related
adverse_reactions.quote: These observations were classified as mild, self-limiting and consisted of 2 incidents of vomition, 2 of depressed appetite and 2 of either diarrhea or soft stool.

adverse_reactions.term: diarrhea or soft stool, judged probably not drug related
adverse_reactions.quote: These observations were classified as mild, self-limiting and consisted of 2 incidents of vomition, 2 of depressed appetite and 2 of either diarrhea or soft stool.

adverse_reactions.term: vomiting (pivotal field trial; two cases led to discontinuation)
adverse_reactions.quote: Vomiting was noted in three enrofloxacin treated dogs, one dog developed diarrhea and one had a decrease in appetite. Two of the vomiting cases resulted in the medication being discontinued and it was judged that the vomiting in these cases was apparently treatment related.

notes: Original NADA 140-441 summary (1988). PK from Ling & Baggot 12-dog study (values reported narratively, no Cmax/AUC figures) plus Table 14 tissue/body fluid distribution (rows quoted as extracted; columns are 2.0/4.0/8.0 h after a single 2.5 mg/kg oral dose). Target animal safety: pivotal margin-of-safety study (1X/3X/5X for 30 days) chosen for design; additional findings from drug tolerance and puppy studies included because articular cartilage lesions are the key finding. Effectiveness pivotal field trial n reflects enrolled dogs; 99 enrofloxacin/66 Tribrissen cases assessed for clinical response and 73/48 for bacteriological response. Adverse reaction counts in the pivotal trial are spelled out in words (three, one) so treated left null for that row; control group: no reported side effects in the Tribrissen group.

product_name:
Baytril™ Antibacterial Tablets
Baytril™ Taste Tabs™ Antibacterial Tablets

indication.text: Management of disease associated with bacteria susceptible to enrofloxacin (cats and dogs).
indication.quote: Indication: For the management of disease associated with bacteria susceptible to enrofloxacin.

dose_regimen.dose: Dogs 5-20 mg/kg (2.27 to 9.07 mg/lb); cats 5 mg/kg (2.27 mg/lb)
dose_regimen.frequency: single daily dose or divided into two equal daily doses at 12 hour intervals
dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: cat dose lowered to 5 mg/kg/day due to post-approval reports of retinal toxicity; do not exceed 5 mg/kg/day in cats
dose_regimen.quote: Cats: Administer orally at 5 mg/kg (2.27 mg/lb) of body weight. The dose for dogs and cats may be administered either as a single daily dose or divided into two (2) equal daily doses administered at twelve (12) hour intervals. Dogs: Administer orally at a rate to provide 5-20 mg/kg (2.27 to 9.07 mg/lb) of body weight.

target_animal_safety.duration: 21 consecutive days (groups observed for 3 or 5 weeks)

findings.finding: Vomiting, salivation and depression at 20 and 50 mg/kg/day
findings.quote: Vomiting, salivation and depression were noted in the 20 and 50 mg/kg/day groups.

findings.finding: 5 mg/kg/day: normal ophthalmic exams and ERGs, no retinal histopathology
findings.quote: Cats receiving 5 mg/kg/day of enrofloxacin had normal ophthalmic exams and no abnormalities noted on the electroretinograms (ERGs) throughout the study.

findings.finding: 20 mg/kg/day: 2 of 8 cats abnormal ERGs; two other cats with serious fundic lesions (retinal degeneration)
findings.quote: In the 20 mg/kg/day groups, 2 of 8 cats had abnormal findings on ERGs.

findings.finding: 50 mg/kg/day: 5 of 8 cats with generalized retinal degeneration; irreversible histopathological retinal changes in all 8
findings.quote: In the 50 mg/kg/day groups, 5 out of 8 cats had serious fundic lesions consisting of generalized retinal degeneration.

findings.finding: Conclusion: 5 mg/kg/day should not be exceeded in cats because higher doses may cause retinal toxicity
findings.quote: It was concluded that a dose of 5 mg/kg/day should not be exceeded in cats as higher doses may cause retinal toxicity.

target_animal_safety.design_quote: BAYTRIL was administered orally at 5 mg/kg, 20 mg/kg, and 50 mg/kg of body weight per day for 21 consecutive days. b. Animals: Thirty-two (32) healthy cats (16 males and 16 females) were randomly assigned to four treatment groups of 4 cats/sex/group.

adverse_reactions.term: Ocular: mydriasis, retinal degeneration, loss of vision (post-approval reports, cats)
adverse_reactions.quote: Ocular: Mydriasis, retinal degeneration (retinal atrophy, attenuated retinal vessels, and hyperreflective tapeta have been reported), loss of vision.

adverse_reactions.term: Gastrointestinal: vomiting, anorexia, elevated liver enzymes, diarrhea (post-approval reports)
adverse_reactions.quote: Gastrointestinal: vomiting, anorexia, elevated liver enzymes, diarrhea

adverse_reactions.term: Behavioral: depression, lethargy, vocalization, aggression (post-approval reports)

notes: 2001 supplement to a dog/cat application; the only new study is a feline ocular safety study (target_animal_safety records CATS, not dogs: 32 cats at 0, 5, 20 and 50 mg/kg/day = control, 1X, 4X, 10X for 21 days). Dog dose range 5-20 mg/kg unchanged. No new effectiveness data (cross-referenced to earlier summaries). Adverse reactions are voluntary post-approval adverse drug experience reports listed in labeling without rates.

indication.text: Treatment of dermal infections (wounds and abscesses), respiratory infections and urinary tract infections (cystitis) in dogs caused by susceptible strains of E. coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Proteus mirabilis and Staphylococcus aureus; supplement removes the contraindication against use in breeding female dogs.
indication.quote: This supplemental application amends the NADA to remove the contradiction against use in breeding female dogs.

dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: two to three days beyond cessation of clinical signs to a maximum of ten days
dose_regimen.quote: The optimum oral dose of Baytril® (brand of enrofloxacin) Tablets has been established at 2.5 mg/kg (1.13 mg/lb) of body weight administered twice daily.

target_animal_safety.duration: 10 consecutive days at each of 4 stages of reproduction (prior to breeding, early pregnancy, late pregnancy, lactation)
target_animal_safety.n_animals: 15 adult female Beagle dogs (four controls, 5 at 5 mg/kg/day, 6 at 15 mg/kg/day)

findings.finding: All reproductive parameters within normal ranges and comparable to historical controls
findings.quote: As shown in the table all the parameters measured were within normal anticipated ranges and are comparable to the historical control results.

findings.finding: No adverse effects on reproductive parameters and no clinical signs of toxicosis at up to 3X the labeled rate for 10 days at 4 reproductive stages
findings.quote: The study concluded that no adverse effects occurred upon reproductive parameters nor were there any clinical signs of toxicosis when female breeding dogs are treated with enrofloxacin tablets at doses as high as 3 times the labeled rate for 10 consecutive days at 4 critical stages of reproduction: 30 to 0 days prior to breeding, early pregnancy (between the 10th and 30th days), late pregnancy (between the 40th and 60th days) and during lactation (the first 28 days).

target_animal_safety.design_quote: A. Stuke and J. Magerkurth of Topeka, Kansas conducted a reproductive safety study in 15 adult female Beagle breed dogs with the 22.7 mg enrofloxacin tablet. The purpose of this study was to evaluate libido and safety in female breeding dogs following multiple treatments with the approved market tablet formulation. Before treatment the dogs were randomly assigned to one of 3 groups. Four dogs served as the non-treated controls, 5 received treatments orally of 2.5 mg/kg (1.13 mg/lb) twice daily for a total of 5 mg/kg (2.27 mg/lb) per day and 6 were treated orally with 7.5 mg/kg (3.40 mg/lb) twice daily for a total of 15 mg/kg (6.80 mg/lb) per day.

notes: 1990 supplement whose sole new study is the female breeding dog reproductive safety study (Table I reproductive performance compared with 1987 historical controls). Effectiveness cross-referenced to the original NADA summary (54 FR 3444); no new effectiveness data. Indication quote uses the 'Effect of Supplement' sentence because the indication text in this summary is interrupted by a footnote about Klebsiella; the summary's typo 'contradiction' (for contraindication) is preserved.

indication.text: Treatment of dermal infections (wounds and abscesses), respiratory infections (pneumonia, tonsillitis, rhinitis) and urinary cystitis in dogs caused by susceptible strains of E. coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Proteus mirabilis and Staphylococcus aureus.
indication.quote: Baytril® (brand of enrofloxacin) Antibacterial Tablets and Injectable Solution are indicated for the treatment of the following bacterial infections in dogs: Dermal infections (wounds and abscesses) caused by susceptible strains of Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae *, Proteus mirabilis, and Staphylococcus aureus. Respiratory infections (pneumonia, tonsillitis, rhinitis) caused by susceptible strains of Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus. Urinary cystitis caused by susceptible strains of Escherichia coli, Proteus mirabilis and Staphylococcus aureus.

dose_regimen.route: intramuscular (IM) injection as the initial dose, then oral tablets
dose_regimen.frequency: single IM dose followed by tablets every 12 hours
dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: tablets continued twice daily for two to three days beyond cessation of clinical signs to a maximum of ten days
dose_regimen.quote: The optimum dose of Baytril (brand of enrofloxacin) has been established at 2.5 mg/kg (1.13 mg/lb) of body weight administered twice daily (every 12 hours). Baytril Tablets should be given twice daily for two to three days beyond the cessation of clinical signs to a maximum of ten days. Baytril Injectable Solution may be used as the initial dose. It should be administered intramuscularly (IM) as a single dose, followed by Baytril Tablets every 12 hours.

pharmacokinetics.value: serum enrofloxacin after IM injectable: 0.72, 1.09, 1.00, 0.94, 0.82, 0.54, 0.20, 0.10 (units not stated in extracted table)
pharmacokinetics.conditions: Table 1 bioequivalency crossover study, 24 dogs, 2.27% injectable IM at 2.5 mg/kg; columns are pretreatment then 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00, 2.0, 4.0, 8.0 and 12.0 hours after treatment

pharmacokinetics.value: serum enrofloxacin after oral tablet: 0.08, 0.47, 0.70, 0.70, 0.70, 0.55, 0.18, 0.09 (units not stated in extracted table)
pharmacokinetics.conditions: Table 1, same 24 dogs, tablet 2.5 mg/kg oral; columns as above

pharmacokinetics.value: injectable serum levels higher than tablet only in the first hour (P<0.01); no other significant differences
pharmacokinetics.conditions: crossover comparison of AUC, Cmax, Tmax with 90% confidence intervals
pharmacokinetics.quote: Other than the first hour when the injectable values were higher (P<0.01), there were no significant differences between the tablet and injectable group.

pharmacokinetics.value: injectable at least as bioavailable as the tablet
pharmacokinetics.conditions: 2.5 mg/kg single dose, IM vs oral, 24 dogs crossover
pharmacokinetics.quote: Based upon this approach, the injectable formulation is at least as bioavailable as the tablet formulation.

target_animal_safety.duration: 30 days total (3 IM injections then oral tablets twice daily; 3x the labeled duration)
target_animal_safety.n_animals: 16 adult Beagle dogs in groups of 4 (4 nontreated controls)

findings.finding: No adverse effects in any parameter at 1X, 3X or 5X for 3X duration; adequate safety margin
findings.quote: No adverse effects occurred in any of the parameters and the study concluded an adequate safety margin based upon treatment at 5 times the use rate for 3 times the labeled duration.

findings.finding: Drug tolerance at 25x (62.5 mg/kg IM): excitation, incoordination, recumbency, convulsions, tremors, salivation, vomition, depression in 2 dogs, normal within 24 hours
findings.quote: Signs of toxicosis in the 2 treated dogs included excitation, incoordination, recumbency, convulsions, muscle tremors, salivation, vomition, alterations in respiratory rate, and slight to severe depression, but both were clinically normal within 24 hours post-treatment.

findings.finding: Local tolerance: single IM injection of 2.27% formulation caused no tissue swelling or clinically significant lesions
findings.quote: No tissue swelling occurred and no clinically significant lesions were present at necropsy. Histology readings indicated adequate healing.

target_animal_safety.design_quote: M. Kohlenberg of Shawnee Mission, Kansas conducted a study in 16 adult, male and female Beagle dogs in groups of 4 with a combination of the 2.27% injectable formulation intended for market and the approved 22.7 mg tablet currently being marketed. The purpose of this study was to evaluate for clinical signs and histopathology following dosing at 1, 3, and 5x doses for a 3x duration.

effectiveness.design: Pivotal well-controlled, blinded multi-site clinical field trial (March-May 1988); dogs with naturally occurring dermal, otic, respiratory, enteric or urinary infections randomized to enrofloxacin 2.27% injectable (single IM injection at 1 mL/9.1 kg) followed by tablets 2.5 mg/kg BID for up to ten days, versus Tribrissen injection followed by tablets (positive control)
effectiveness.n_dogs: 115 evaluated clinically (61 enrofloxacin, 54 positive control) of 128 enrolled
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: percentage reduction in clinical score (0-4) by body system, pathogen elimination on post-treatment culture, and subjective evaluations
effectiveness.result: Enrofloxacin had a medically significant effect on lesions comparable to Tribrissen (e.g. dermal 84.8% vs 80.6% score reduction); 74 of 99 isolates (74.7%) eliminated vs 46 of 71 (64.8%) for Tribrissen; no drug-related side effects
effectiveness.quote: Of the 128 dogs initially selected, 13 were omitted from any assessment because of protocol deviations that could be expected to influence the results. Clinical evaluations subsequently were conducted on 115 dogs, 61 dosed with enrofloxacin and 54 with the positive control.

adverse_reactions.term: drug related side effects (pivotal clinical trial)
adverse_reactions.quote: No drug related side effects were reported following dosing with either enrofloxacin or Tribrissen.

adverse_reactions.term: moderate tissue swelling at injection site (laboratory/clinical safety evaluation, 88 enrofloxacin dogs)
adverse_reactions.quote: With the injections, there was a 2.3% incidence of moderate tissue swelling following enrofloxacin treatment and a 32.1% incidence of slight to moderate pain following the Tribrissen injections.
Two cases of emesis were observed following treatment with each of the 2 products.

adverse_reactions.term: side effects in field trials (122 enrofloxacin-treated dogs)
adverse_reactions.quote: No side effects were reported in the enrofloxacin treated dogs.

notes: Original NADA 140-913 (injectable) summary, 1990. Section headings were parsed into general_information. PK: Table 1 of the tablet-vs-injectable bioequivalency crossover study is quoted as extracted; the table title was garbled by PDF extraction ('Summary of Daily Gain/Chick') and concentration units are not stated in the extracted text (values appear to be serum enrofloxacin, presumably mcg/mL). Table 2 case distribution header repeats 'Enrofloxacin' for the Tribrissen columns (extraction artifact). Control-group figure for tissue swelling not reported (32.1% refers to pain after Tribrissen injections, a different term).

indication.text: Treatment of canine otitis externa complicated by bacterial and fungal organisms susceptible to enrofloxacin and/or silver sulfadiazine.
indication.quote: for the treatment of canine otitis externa complicated by bacterial and fungal organisms susceptible to enrofloxacin and/or silver sulfadiazine.

dose_regimen.dose: 5-10 drops per treatment (dogs 35 lbs or less); 10-15 drops per treatment (dogs over 35 lbs); each mL contains 5 mg enrofloxacin and 10 mg silver sulfadiazine
dose_regimen.quote: Each mL contains 5 mg enrofloxacin and 10 mg silver sulfadiazine. Route of Administration: Baytril® Otic is topically applied to the ear canal. Recommended Dosage: Shake well before each use. Tilt head so that the affected ear is presented in an upward orientation. Administer a sufficient quantity of Baytril® Otic to coat the aural lesions and the external auditory canal. As a general guide, administer 5-10 drops per treatment in dogs weighing 35 lbs. or less, and 10-15 drops per treatment in dogs weighing more than 35 lbs. Following treatment, gently massage the ear so as to ensure complete and uniform distribution of the medication throughout the external ear canal. Apply twice daily for a duration of up to 14 days.

target_animal_safety.duration: 42 consecutive days (3X the labeled duration); 60-day study
target_animal_safety.n_animals: twelve male and twelve female beagle dogs (four per sex per dose group) plus four male and four female vehicle controls

findings.finding: Mild aural erythema in all dogs of all groups (including controls), onset day 1-2, resolved within 2 days of stopping treatment; no edema
findings.quote: The most notable clinical abnormality was aural erythema. This affected all dogs in the study, and occurred to the same extent in all treatment groups.

findings.finding: No changes in hearing
findings.quote: No changes in hearing were reported.

findings.finding: No clinically significant hematology or clinical chemistry changes
findings.quote: No clinically significant changes were reported for hematology or clinical chemistry values.

findings.finding: Up to 5X dose volume for 42 days produced only reversible ear erythema; no other adverse effects
findings.quote: Twice daily administration of Baytril® Otic at doses up to five times the recommended dose volume and for as long as 42 days produced reversible erythema of the ears. No other adverse effects or signs of toxicity were reported.

target_animal_safety.design_quote: To determine the safety of Baytril® Otic when 10 (1X), 30 (3X), or 50 (5X) drops are administered into the ear canals of dogs twice a day for 42 consecutive days.

effectiveness.design: Controlled, double-blind, multi-site (7 veterinary hospitals) placebo-controlled clinical field study in dogs with naturally occurring otitis externa (clinical score >= 6); ototopical treatment twice daily for 7-14 days, ~2:1 active:placebo randomization
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: clinical success: final composite otic clinical score of 2 or less, assessed 3-4 days after the last dose
effectiveness.result: Therapeutic success in 67% of aural infections treated with active formulation vs 14% with placebo (p = 0.0143) after 14 days; odds of success 14.78 times greater with active product
effectiveness.quote: By study conclusion, 113 (67%) and 56 (33%) cases had been randomly assigned to the Baytril® Otic and placebo treatment groups, respectively (approximately a 2:1 active: placebo ratio).

adverse_reactions.term: local hypersensitivity-type reaction (aural erythema, swelling, vesicles, pain or pruritus after 2-3 days; resolved on withdrawal)
adverse_reactions.quote: Two of 113 cases (1.8%) treated with Baytril® Otic displayed responses compatible with a local hypersensitivity reaction to one of the components within the formulation.

notes: Original NADA 141-176 (2000). No systemic PK study in the summary (only in vitro MIC and FICI data), so pharmacokinetics left empty. Field study enrolled 169 dogs in total ('One hundred and sixty-nine dogs qualified for study enrollment'); n_dogs gives the 113/56 randomization split. Success rates per site are per ear (122/183 ears active vs 13/93 placebo). Target animal safety n given in words because the summary spells the numbers out ('Twelve male and twelve female beagle dogs'); adverse-reaction 'treated' expressed as 1.8% of 113 cases since 'Two' is spelled out in the quote.
